title: Lore Library
description: Ingram, 2026-09-13: 'a small set of documents which you treat as holy.' The curated registry of documents Claude must check before making a writing decision, and Ingram browses/edits through the Gazetteer's Lore mode. Deliberately NOT every file in the repo -- adding a document here is a decision that it belongs in the small set, not an automatic index of everything. importance mirrors data/schema/location.schema.json's rank ladder: 1 is read fully before anything remotely related is written, and any ambiguous edit to it must be asked about rather than inferred (design/location-rank.md's rank-1 rule, extended to documents); 5 is background reference, fine to skim or edit on reasonable judgement. Consumed by tools/gazetteer/core/lore_library.py.

id.description: Stable short id, kebab-case -- independent of path, so a file move doesn't orphan instructions/backlinks pointing at it.

path.description: Repo-relative path to the real markdown (or JSON) file. The library is an index, not a copy -- content always comes from this file.

importance.description: 1 = holy: read in full before anything related is written, any ambiguous edit gets asked about, never edited on inference alone. 5 = background reference. Mirrors location.schema.json's rank ladder on purpose -- same concept, applied to documents instead of places.

category.description: Broad shelf, for the library's own grouping -- not a rigid taxonomy.

description.description: One line: what this document is for, and when to check it.

topics.description: Free-text keywords (e.g. 'schools', 'the-watcher', 'nozomi') so a location or NPC write can be matched against relevant documents without reading every title.
